introduction: Legal Services Alabama offers free civil legal help to qualifying low-income residents. Intake staff review both financial eligibility and the legal problem before deciding what assistance is available.

who: Applicants must meet the organization’s current eligibility rules. Income guidelines are updated, so ask intake staff about the rule for your household.
LSA handles civil matters; its offices do not handle criminal cases. Limited resources mean not every eligible case can be accepted.
sections.get: The organization can provide civil legal assistance and may refer an unaccepted case to another resource. Its practice includes housing, consumer and public-benefit problems; the help offered depends on case review.
sections.docs: Prepare the names of the people involved, income information and relevant letters or court papers. Put a hearing, filing deadline or eviction date at the top of your notes. These are preparation tips; intake staff determine what must be submitted.
sections.apply:
1. Use the Apply Online option on LSA’s website or call 866-456-4995. Spanish-language callers can use 888-835-3505.
  2. Explain the legal problem, your location and any court deadline. Answer intake questions so staff can check eligibility and conflicts.
  3. If you plan to visit an office, call first. Keep the intake reference and follow the instructions for sending documents.
sections.after: Ask whether the organization has agreed to represent you and what tasks remain your responsibility. Do not assume an intake request postpones a court deadline. If the case is not accepted, ask staff about referrals or available clinics.

faqs: No. Its offices handle civil cases. Ask intake staff for a suitable referral if your problem falls outside its services.
Is submitting the intake form the same as having a lawyer?
No. Wait for an explicit acceptance and explanation of the services offered.
What if I have a hearing soon?
Give intake staff the date immediately and keep track of court obligations while the request is being reviewed.
What happens if LSA cannot take my case?
Its FAQ says staff can provide information about other resources, including volunteer lawyer programs and clinics.
